RTX Stock Update: Rises 0.51%, Up 1.4% in Five Sessions
sum: Technical analysis of RTX stock on November 11, 2026: price 201.29 USD, trend uptrend, RSI 57.4, support 186.95, resistance 203.82.

RTX Corporation closed Wednesday's session at $201.29, up 0.51% from a prior close of $200.27, and the move capped a 1.44% gain over five days and a 7.95% rise across the past month. The detail drawing attention is a fresh golden cross: the 20-day average slipped above the 50-day average three sessions before the latest one, while price pulled back to the 20-day line without losing it.

A golden cross is a crossover in which a shorter-term average of closing prices rises through a longer-term one. It does not predict anything by itself. It records that recent prices have averaged higher than prices over the longer span, which is what a sustained advance looks like in the arithmetic.

The 20-day simple moving average (SMA20) stands at $195.75 and the 50-day (SMA50) at $192.92. The gap between them is under three dollars, so the cross is recent and the lines have not yet pulled far apart. The 20-day average rose 1.37% over five days, a measure of how quickly the recent price base is lifting. It is the average's slope, not the stock's own gain.

As the chart shows, price sits above both averages in a stock that has climbed for a month. Over the past 20 sessions it has held between support at $186.95 and resistance at $203.82, and the latest close sits about 85% of the way up that range. That is near the top of the band, which means the market is testing the upper edge rather than drifting in the middle.

The longer view is more restrained. The three-month range runs from a low of $179.02 to a high of $226.41, so RTX remains well below its recent peak even after this month's rally. The advance is a recovery within a wider range, not a breakout to new highs.

Momentum indicators give a measured reading rather than an excited one. The 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI), which scores the pace of recent gains against losses on a 0–100 scale, is 57.4, classed as neutral. Readings above 70 are conventionally seen as stretched; this one has room to run before it signals that. The Stochastic oscillator, which shows where the close sits within its recent high-low range, reads %K 75.8 against %D 64.7.

RTX Corporation stock heads into Baird conference after raised outlook
sum: RTX Corporation is heading into a scheduled investor appearance after reporting strong third-quarter growth and raising its full-year outlook. Chief Financial Officer Neil Mitchill is due to speak at the Baird 2026 Global Industrial Conference on Tuesday, November 10, at 10:05 a.m. Eastern Time, according to RTX.

The company said the presentation will be broadcast live on its website and archived afterward. For investors, the appearance follows the October 20 release of third-quarter results and could provide further commentary on demand, production and execution against the upgraded targets.

RTX reported third-quarter sales of 25.0 billion US dollars, an 11 percent increase from the prior-year period. Adjusted earnings per share reached 2.26 US dollars, up 33 percent, while reported diluted earnings per share was 1.89 US dollars.

The company also reported a 340 billion US dollar backlog, comprising 176 billion US dollars in commercial programs and 164 billion US dollars in defense. More than 81 billion US dollars of new commercial and defense awards during the quarter supported the backlog, according to the RTX third-quarter release.

RTX raised its 2026 adjusted sales outlook to 97.0 billion to 97.5 billion US dollars from 95.0 billion to 96.0 billion US dollars previously. The adjusted earnings-per-share range increased to 7.65 to 7.75 US dollars from 7.10 to 7.25 US dollars, while the free-cash-flow forecast moved to 9.0 billion to 9.2 billion US dollars from 8.50 billion to 8.75 billion US dollars.

All three major businesses contributed to the quarter's sales growth, but profitability trends differed. Collins Aerospace sales increased 10 percent and adjusted operating profit rose 50 percent to 1.788 billion US dollars. Raytheon sales advanced 14 percent and adjusted operating profit increased 32 percent to 1.134 billion US dollars.

Pratt & Whitney sales grew 10 percent, driven mainly by commercial aftermarket demand. Its reported operating profit fell 19 percent to 608 million US dollars, reflecting a 363 million US dollar charge related to a customer bankruptcy. On an adjusted basis, operating profit increased 29 percent to 968 million US dollars. That distinction matters for investors assessing recurring execution rather than one-off effects.

RTX’s Raytheon Wins DARPA Contract – Everything That Investors Need To Know
sum: RTX’s (RTX) Raytheon business was awarded a Phase 1 contract from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to develop an all-optical signal processing system under its Photonic Integrated Circuit Architectures for Scalable System Objectives (PICASSO) program.

“By moving critical processing entirely into the optical domain, we can enable significantly faster response times for a broad range of applications,” said Colin Whelan, president of Advanced Technology at Raytheon.

Under the contract, Raytheon’s Advanced Technology team will design and demonstrate photonic circuit technology that uses light rather than electricity to process signals. The technology is intended to help operators detect threats sooner and maintain situational awareness in contested environments.

Current photonic circuits convert optical signals into electrical signals for further processing. Raytheon says eliminating that conversion step can help preserve signal strength and integrity as circuits become smaller and more complex.

Raytheon is working with Synopsys, which will provide design and simulation tools for the project. The company will draw on its experience in photonics process development, radio-frequency design, and military systems to advance all-optical processing technology.

On October 15, RTX announced that its Raytheon business had been selected to modernize U.S. Space Force radar sites under the Ground-Based Radar Digitization (GBRD) program. The upgrades are intended to improve radar performance and reliability while strengthening early-warning and space-monitoring capabilities.

Raytheon will work with the Space Force and industry partners to develop a common, open architecture designed to improve sustainment efficiency, reduce vendor lock-in, and simplify future upgrades. The program will deliver prototype solutions before transitioning to rapid fielding at the remaining locations.

sum: Micro-Star International is adding new AI hardware to its product portfolio. MSI's Prestige N16 Flip AI+ and Prestige N16 are included in NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptop launch, while the company is shipping its XpertStation WS300 through ASI, D&H and Newegg.

Ava Fund reports that the RTX Spark systems combine NVIDIA graphics and AI computing in premium Windows PCs. MSI's two listed models give the Taiwanese hardware maker a presence in the initial product lineup, alongside systems from other major PC brands.

The XpertStation WS300 addresses a different part of the AI market. According to the same report, the deskside system is based on NVIDIA DGX Station architecture and uses NVIDIA's GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip. MSI positions the machine for AI development, model fine-tuning and local inference.

The product is being distributed through ASI, D&H and Newegg. That channel setup gives the launch access to enterprise and specialist technology buyers, although the available report does not provide sales figures or financial guidance tied to the product.

MSI's investor information identifies the company as a developer and supplier of digital products and lists stock code 2377. The company describes its focus as innovation, product quality and shareholder value. Its broader portfolio includes gaming and professional-creation hardware.

MSI develops and sells motherboards, graphics cards, notebooks, monitors, desktops, networking equipment, servers and related peripherals. It also offers AIoT solutions and serves customers across Asia, Europe and the United States, with its headquarters in New Taipei City, Taiwan. In computer hardware, MSI competes with broader global brands such as Apple, Dell Technologies and Samsung Electronics while maintaining a stronger specialization in gaming and enthusiast PC components.

The company-specific developments add product visibility in AI-enabled PCs and enterprise computing. For investors, the next key questions are customer adoption, shipment volumes and whether the new systems contribute materially to revenue and margins.

Revenue expectations follow a similar pattern, with consensus estimates pointing to 8.5% sales growth for RTX against a still-solid but comparatively modest 6.4% for GD.
Both companies have seen their EPS estimates for 2026 and 2027 revised upward over the past 60 days, signaling that analyst confidence across the sector is rising.
A $100 million expansion of Pratt & Whitney’s Rzeszów facility in Poland, announced in October 2026, illustrates the scale of manufacturing investment RTX is deploying to meet future demand.

sum: RTX, (NYSE:RTX) Industrials RTX Corporation (NYSE:RTX) 202.83 USD +3.030 1.517% Last Updated at: 2026-11-02T21:04:00Z the aerospace and defense giant behind Collins Aerospace, Pratt and Whitney and Raytheon, delivered one of the strongest reports of the industrial earnings season. Sales grew at a double-digit rate across commercial and defense businesses, the backlog reached a record and management raised its full-year guidance. Defense demand surged as the company secured large multi-year missile contracts. Aerospace and defense stocks across the NYSE Composite have been supported by rising military budgets and recovering air travel, and RTX's results captured both trends.

Sales rose at a double-digit rate from a year earlier, with organic growth even slightly faster. Adjusted earnings per share increased sharply and beat analyst expectations by a wide margin. Reported earnings included acquisition accounting adjustments, restructuring costs and a charge linked to a customer bankruptcy.
Operating cash flow and free cash flow were lower than the prior-year quarter, partly due to timing, but the company raised its full-year free cash flow outlook.

RTX ended the quarter with a record backlog, split between commercial aerospace and defense. The backlog grew sharply from both the prior year and the prior quarter. New awards across commercial and defense businesses during the quarter were very large, far exceeding quarterly sales.

sum: RTX Corp (RTX) moved down by 3.47%. The Industrial Goods sector is up by 0.89%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Bloom Energy Corp (BE) up 9.16%; Rocket Lab USA Inc (RKLB) down 2.71%; Caterpillar Inc (CAT) up 3.41%.

The downward movement and significant intraday volatility observed in RTX Corporation shares were primarily driven by a dramatic shift in the global geopolitical landscape. The signing of a peace agreement between the United States and Iran, which effectively resolved their conflict and reopened the Strait of Hormuz, led to a substantial decline in global crude oil prices. This positive step toward peace in the Middle East significantly eased the geopolitical risk premium that had previously supported defense sector valuations. As a result, institutional investors engaged in a sector-wide rotation out of defensive and aerospace-defense equities, triggering a broad pullback in major defense contractors like RTX, despite the company's strong long-term fundamentals.

Furthermore, the macroeconomic environment influenced the day's market dynamics. While the broader Wall Street indexes rebounded, the gains were heavily concentrated in high-growth technology and semiconductor stocks. The Federal Reserve’s hawkish undertones from its recent meeting, where policymakers signaled the possibility of raising interest rates later in the year, continued to weigh on capital-intensive industrials. Because RTX is heavily committed to capital-intensive capacity expansions, including its recently announced investment upgrade at its Rhode Island facility to accelerate radar testing, the prospect of prolonged high borrowing costs increases execution risks and pressures valuation multiples.

Lastly, investor focus has increasingly transitioned from securing order demand to manufacturing execution. Despite robust demand tailwinds, including news that Finland authorized the purchase of Raytheon-manufactured precision-guided glide bombs to support its fighter jet fleet, the market is pricing in the challenges of converting a record backlog into actual earnings. Issues surrounding the aerospace supply chain and high-margin engine maintenance programs remain active concerns.
